takeaway: Ca 15-3 breast, Ca 19-9 advanced colorectal, VMA phaeochromocytoma, ADH oat cell are correct. Calcitonin marks medullary thyroid carcinoma; parathyroid carcinoma raises PTH.

question.text: The following tumour markers are correctly paired with an associated neoplasia except which one?

lines.text: Check each pair. Ca 15-3 goes with breast cancer, and Ca 19-9 with advanced colorectal carcinoma.
Antidiuretic hormone goes with oat cell tumours.
Now the parathyroid. Parathyroid carcinoma may increase parathyroid hormone, PTH.
It is not marked by calcitonin.
Calcitonin belongs to the thyroid, in medullary carcinoma.
So the pair that does not fit is calcitonin with parathyroid carcinoma.
